rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the baseline performance of RNA-only modeling with PCA encoding and single-profile setting. It clarifies whether RNA data alone can achieve competitive accuracy, isolating the impact of the rna_encoder and profile_setting. This is the best first step to establish a performance benchmark before exploring more complex multimodal configurations.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only single-profile models with PCA encoding achieve moderate accuracy (0.4849). This experiment tests whether using a multiprofile setting with average pooling aggregation improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of key design choices (multi-profile) with minimal changes (same RNA encoder, no image data), providing critical insight into whether these factors matter without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) with avgpool aggregation. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping multiprofile and avgpool) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of critical design decisions without changing multiple factors, leveraging the strong evidence for multiprofile/avgpool as a baseline.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile setups (config_002/005) outperform singleprofile, and scvi_n200 (config_005) beats pca_n2000. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation (vs avgpool in config_005) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising multiprofile/scvi combination while exploring a key design choice with minimal additional complexity.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation outperform singleprofile and pca_n2000. This experiment tests scgpt encoder (a new RNA encoder) in multiprofile setting with avgpool, isolating the impact of encoder choice while maintaining the promising profile and aggregation settings from config_005/006. It balances exploration of new encoders with exploitation of established effective components.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline, using the same transformer aggregation and concat fusion. It isolates the effect of multimodal integration, which is critical for determining if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This balances exploitation of the top RNA-only setup with exploration of multimodal potential, addressing a key design choice with minimal additional complexity.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (like config_032) outperform RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether changing fusion strategy from concat to weighted in config_032 (which already uses transformer aggregation) clarifies if weighted fusion improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion method while building on the strong foundation of config_032's RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation choice.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more complex model) and the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced architecture) further improves performance. It isolates the impact of these key components while maintaining the proven aggregation/fusion strategy, balancing exploration of advanced encoders with exploitation of prior success.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50, using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other components (scvi_n200, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) the same would improve performance. This isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical design choice, and leverages the strong prior evidence for the RNA encoder and fusion method.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of changing fusion from weighted to concat while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the impact of fusion method. It clarifies whether the fusion strategy is critical, a key design choice, and avoids redundant changes.
